title: Compliance: dos, don'ts and the final check
objectives: Apply the module's compliance rules to any withdrawal plan.
Pass the trainer's final check: rate, inflation, sequence, gaps, buckets, SWP, reviews, behaviour and compliance.
body_md:
Do: base the plan on actual expenses, other income and the whole corpus. Show how long the money may last as an illustration, with assumptions. Call an SWP a withdrawal plan, not guaranteed income. Explain that SWP withdrawals are redemptions that may be taxed; refer to a CA. Recommend health cover and nominee checks. Record the plan, buckets and review date.

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Base the plan on actual expenses, other income and the whole corpus | Set an SWP amount without knowing the client's spending |
| Show how long the money may last as an illustration, with assumptions | Promise the corpus will last a set number of years |
| Call an SWP a withdrawal plan, not guaranteed income | Present an SWP as “monthly income” or “pension” without caveats |
| Explain that SWP withdrawals are redemptions that may be taxed; refer to a CA | Say SWP income is tax-free |
| Recommend health cover and nominee checks | Ignore risks outside the portfolio |
| Record the plan, buckets and review date | Change withdrawals without the client's documented agreement |

> **Investor takeaway:** Standard disclaimer: mutual fund investments are subject to market risks; read all scheme-related documents carefully. Past performance does not guarantee future returns. Final check for trainers: a new joiner passes this module when they can explain withdrawal rate, inflation and sequence-of-returns risk in plain words; estimate how long a corpus may last at different withdrawal rates (illustratively); gather the facts needed to plan a client's withdrawals; set up a bucket structure and an SWP; review and adjust withdrawals each year; and handle overspending and panic in falls, within compliance. All figures in this module are illustrative calculations with stated assumptions, not forecasts.
example: A trainee bases the plan on expenses, income and the whole corpus, shows illustrations with assumptions, and records the plan, buckets and review date.
say: Base the plan on actual expenses, other income and the whole corpus.
Call an SWP a withdrawal plan, not guaranteed income.
never: Set an SWP amount without knowing the client's spending.

check.q: A retired client wants to give ₹15 L to her son. How do you handle it?
o: Show the effect on her withdrawal rate and plan; discuss options; it is her decision, documented
Ignore the effect on the plan
Fund it from the monthly SWP
